scope: security-agent-dev (scanner and report); supabase/migrations/ in each affected project repo; the Supabase projects behind them via the supabase MCP or CLI

requirements.requirement: docs/rls-remediation-2026-10-06.md lists every scanned project and every public-schema table found with RLS off, with columns project, table, sensitive yes/no, action taken, and status fixed/excluded-with-reason — check: test -f docs/rls-remediation-2026-10-06.md && grep -qi "status" docs/rls-remediation-2026-10-06.md
requirements.expected: Report lists every scanned project and every RLS-off public table with project, table, sensitive, action taken, status fixed/excluded-with-reason
requirements.method: node scripts/rls-report.mjs from the baseline scan + lane results + after-scan; then the capsule check command; a row audit that every fixed row has access path, migration, anon-after and app-path-after filled
requirements.observed: Report has 112 rows (every RLS-off public table from the 45-project baseline scan, 22 projects), columns project | table | sensitive | anon before | access path found | action taken | migration | anon after | app path after | status. Totals: fixed 109, excluded 3 (shipsafe_demo_customers: intentional demo fixture; 2x PostGIS spatial_ref_sys: extension-owned, owner supabase_admin), open 0. Scope notes list the 31 paused projects (not scannable) and the MobileGo Java backend (Heroku, not Supabase, excluded and untouched). Check command printed C1-PASS. Row audit: 112 rows, 0 fixed rows missing a field.

evidence.command: test -f docs/rls-remediation-2026-10-06.md && grep -qi "status" docs/rls-remediation-2026-10-06.md && echo C1-PASS

requirements.requirement: A rerunnable scan script exists in security-agent-dev and its latest output, saved next to the report, shows zero public-schema tables with RLS off outside the documented exclusions — check: ls docs/ | grep -qi "rls-scan"
requirements.expected: Rerunnable scan script; latest output next to the report shows 0 RLS-off public tables outside documented exclusions
requirements.method: node scripts/rls-scan.mjs --out docs/rls-scan-2026-10-06-after (read-only; pg_class.relrowsecurity + grants via Management API, every RLS-off table probed with every anon-role key)
requirements.observed: After-scan 2026-10-06T21:38:11Z over 45 live projects, 0 scan errors: 3 public tables with RLS off, exactly the 3 documented exclusions (e2e-test-app shipsafe_demo_customers; IslandFlow and MGO Management Dashboard spatial_ref_sys). Baseline was 112. ls docs | grep rls-scan lists before/after .json/.md; check printed C2-PASS.

evidence.command: node scripts/rls-scan.mjs --out docs/rls-scan-2026-10-06-after; ls docs/ | grep -qi "rls-scan" && echo C2-PASS

requirements.requirement: For every fixed table, the report records a read using the project's anon key that returns no rows or a permission error, plus one read or write of the owning app's normal path that still succeeds
requirements.expected: Each fixed table: anon read returns no rows or a permission error; the owning app's normal path still succeeds
requirements.method: Per-lane proofs recorded per row (anon after / app path after), then an independent re-check with scripts/rls-verify.mjs: every anon-role key (legacy anon JWT + publishable) and the server key (service_role/secret) against each of the 109 fixed tables
requirements.observed: rls-verify: anon lock-out 109 pass / 0 fail (401, or 200/206 with 0 rows); server-key read 109/109 readable, 41,564 rows. Lane app-path proofs per row: service_role/postgres counts matching baseline for server-side apps (facegate live server connects as postgres; primer drizzle as postgres), simulated authenticated users for Grab & Go client tables (e.g. pin_auth_sessions own 28 / stranger 0; order_modification_requests customer 1 / owner 1 / stranger 0), live HTTP: primer.rocksteady.ai/proposal/<approved token> 200 + bogus 404; gts-statements-next /view/<expired token> 200 'Link Expired' on the new service-role deploy while the old anon-key deploy now 404s; techsupport.gtsbahamas.com RAG rpc as service_role returns 5 rows.

requirements.requirement: Each project changed has a committed migration file under supabase/migrations/ whose name is listed in the report next to its tables
requirements.expected: Every changed project has a committed migration under supabase/migrations/, named in the report beside its tables
requirements.method: git cat-file -e <commit>:<migration path> for every lane result, plus git branch -r --contains for remote presence
requirements.observed: 20 projects changed, 18 migration files (propria-core file covers coral-harbour-pilot; mgosupport file covers brazilnut-support): all present in their commits. Pushed to private remotes for 16 repos (main or sec/rls-lockdown-20261006); the two no-repo projects (Secure Apps, e2e-test-app) are committed under security-agent-dev/supabase/migrations/<project>/ and kept local because that repo is public. facegate's file is in packages/server/supabase/migrations (repo forbids a root folder; the boot runner reads it). Report migration column lists repo/path@commit for every fixed row.

evidence.command: git cat-file -e <commit>:<migration> and git branch -a --contains <commit> for every lane result
